name: Gabapentin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Gabapentin is cleared almost entirely by the kidneys, and its half-life lengthens from about 6.5 hours to 52 hours as kidney function falls. The US label gives total daily doses by creatinine clearance (CrCl) for patients 12 years and older, plus a supplemental dose after each hemodialysis session.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault).

bands.recommendation: 400 to 1400 mg/day in 2 divided doses (label: CrCl >30 to 59).
200 to 700 mg/day as a single daily dose (label: CrCl >15 to 29).
At CrCl 15: 100 to 300 mg/day once daily. Below 15, reduce in proportion to CrCl (for example, CrCl 7.5 gets half the CrCl-15 dose) (label).

hd: Maintenance dose by estimated CrCl, plus a supplemental dose after each 4 hours of hemodialysis: 125, 150, 200, 250 or 350 mg, matched to the maintenance regimen of 100, 125, 150, 200 or 300 mg once daily (label).
pd: No data in label. Insufficient data: use the CrCl <15 regimen with specialist input and watch for sedation.
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
dialyzable: Yes: in anuric adults, half-life about 132 hours off dialysis falls to about 3.8 hours during dialysis (label).
monitoring: Sedation, dizziness, ataxia, confusion and respiratory depression (higher risk with opioids and in kidney impairment).

pediatric.approved_ages: Adjunctive therapy for partial-onset seizures: 3 years and older. Postherpetic neuralgia: not established in children (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Ages 3 to 11: start 10 to 15 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses, titrate over about 3 days; maintenance 40 mg/kg/day (ages 3 to 4) or 25 to 35 mg/kg/day (ages 5 to 11), in 3 divided doses. Ages 12 and older: adult dosing (300 to 600 mg three times daily).
pediatric.max_dose: Up to 50 mg/kg/day was given in a long-term study (label); do not exceed the adult maximum of 3600 mg/day.

renal.recommendation: Ages 12 and older: use the adult CrCl table. Under 12: not studied with kidney impairment (label); specialist input.
Ages 12 and older: adult CrCl table (CrCl >30 to 59: 400 to 1400 mg/day in 2 doses). Under 12: not studied; specialist input.
Ages 12 and older: adult CrCl table (200 to 700 mg/day once daily). Under 12: not studied; specialist input.
Ages 12 and older: adult CrCl table. Under 12: not studied; specialist input.

pediatric.hd: Ages 12 and older: adult post-dialysis supplemental dosing (label). Under 12: not studied.
pediatric.notes: The label's kidney table is written for patients 12 years and older and uses CrCl (Cockcroft–Gault), not bedside Schwartz eGFR.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
